new_jobs.description:
About Northern Trust

As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions.

Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide.

With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service.

Job Summary

An exciting opportunity is now available for a dynamic market leader to lead our Wealth Management business in the Orange County region. The ideal candidate will lead a talented team of experts in delivering our holistic offering to clients related to investment management, trust and estate planning, and private banking.

We are seeking an energetic professional with a demonstrated track record of successful market leadership to oversee, plan and direct activities for the team, ensuring resources are available to accomplish the business objectives.  Additionally, the Senior Managing Director will lead, mentor, coach, recruit, as well as partner to outline overall strategy to reporting managers and employees. This individual will work to attract and retain high-quality talent who contribute to excellent client outcomes and overall business growth. This role is responsible for leading and fostering an environment of development, accountability, mutual respect and teamwork that encourages the dedication and loyalty of employees and clients alike. This role will lead business development and growth activities and will have full accountability for team performance and profitability.

This role includes direct oversight for an impressive team of experienced wealth management advisors as well as matrix management for some employees within those markets that may report through their respective practice areas. This role is vital to the success of our wealth management business in the West Region. This leader is an integral part of the West Region Leadership Team.

Major Duties

Accountability for overall performance of respective market including setting and executing, in collaboration with other leaders, vision for excellence, while incorporating specific strategic plans and objectives of the corporation, business unit and region. This includes accountability for performance management for partners within their hierarchy.

Provide leadership, mentoring, coaching and guidance to staff, fostering an environment which encourages inclusion, employee participation, collaboration, teamwork, and communication. Attracting and retaining talent is a critical priority.

Responsible for client interactions and communications, monitors retention of current clients and broadening of relationships, and may address specific sensitive or complex client needs.

Responsible for expense budgets.

Promote, lead, and participate in attaining sales goals for new business in conjunction with West Region sales and marketing leadership. Engaged in the community representing the Northern Trust brand and sourcing in new business.

Qualifications

10+ years of experience in wealth management leadership roles along with deep knowledge and expertise in trust, banking, and investment management and wealth advisory services.
Successful track record of managing a business (a P&L) and delivering an outstanding client experience.
Candidates should have a demonstrated track record of success in business development and market growth.
Previous experience with Change Management and leading/implementing change.
Proven track record in recruiting and developing top talent.
Ability to outline and drive strategic growth.
Demonstrated experience of deep community involvement including but not limited to board service.
Proven leadership and organizational skills to determine goals, resource needs, and to assess and develop the skills of staff.
Excellent relationship, influencing, decision making, and critical thinking skills are required.
Strong academics, with an advanced degree and relevant credentials preferred.

Salary Range

$236,555 - 414,115 USD

Salary range is a good faith estimate of base pay. Northern Trust provides a comprehensive benefits package including retirement benefits (401k and pension), health and welfare benefits (medical, dental, vision, spending accounts and disability), paid time off, parental and caregiver leave, life & accident insurance, and other voluntary and well-being benefits. Northern Trust also provides a discretionary bonus program that may include an equity component.

Work Authorization

Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. Northern Trust will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work visa status for this opportunity (no sponsorship is available for H-1B, L-1, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, F-1, J-1, OPT, CPT or any other employment-based visa).

Working with Us

As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve.

Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities.

Reasonable Accommodation

Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com, or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.

new_jobs.title: Associate Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Essie Justice Group (Essie) is building grassroots power to dismantle the US incarceration system, the most egregious creator of racial and gender injustice of our time. We are a loving and powerful community of women with incarcerated loved ones. Our community includes cisgender women, transgender women, formerly incarcerated women, gender expansive people, elders, and young people.

After twelve years of building an active membership across California and beyond, Essie is deepening its base-building and leadership development strategies with the 1 in 4 women with incarcerated loved ones to propel bold decarceration agendas across the nation. We seek to transform the criminal legal system and create a Black feminist future rooted in care, equity, community safety, and liberation. In the midst of significant organizational growth, we are seeking an impact-driven and strategic Associate Director of Development to join our team.

As Essie grows, the Associate Director of Development will take the lead in managing the internal operations for our philanthropic efforts to support our work to end mass incarceration and build a Black feminist future. We see our donors as partners in this work, and the Associate Director of Development is a thoughtful and deliberate steward of these relationships. The Associate Director of Development is a strategic fundraising leader who is comfortable getting into the weeds while also balancing the strategic development of the team. They excel at crafting clear and compelling narratives that connect philanthropic partners and potential donors to meaningful movement work, think empathetically about their audiences, and are deeply motivated by a belief in the leadership development and liberation strategies of directly impacted people.

Core Responsibilities

Donor Program Design and Management - Help develop strategies and processes for identifying and engaging donors and nurturing and managing donor relationships.

Partner with the Interim Co-Executive Directors to establish benchmarks and goals for individual fundraising.
Iterate and oversee development infrastructure internally, including CRM features and advising on key changes to roles and make-up of our existing structures for stakeholder engagement.
Evaluate and recommend new funding opportunities in alignment with Essie’s strategic priorities and programmatic work.
Support in determining the key organizational accomplishments and aspirations we communicate in grant applications and reports.
Lead the design and management of prospect research and relevant relationship management processes.
Develop solicitation goals, cultivation strategies, and stewardship plans in a way that donors are respected, retained, and inspired to increase their support.
Develop and implement engagement strategies including, but not limited to: telephone outreach, email/mail outreach, personal visits, and small group activities.
Review and finalize grants and proposals.
Develop strategies and manage implementation of donation appeals (digital or print as strategically identified) including seasonal appeals (ex. end of year/holiday giving) and complementary fundraising appeals matching Essie’s campaigns and policy fights.
Track and report results of appeals and special campaigns, adjusting strategies as needed.

Donor Relationship Stewardship - Manage and facilitate Essie’s ongoing organizational relationships with individual donors, ensuring that they remain engaged in and inspired by Essie’s work.

Manage robust donor stewardship and cultivation touchpoints including personal thank yous, digital communications, and personalized outreach.
Prepare and distribute materials to communicate with supporters including thank you letters, event reports, and annual reports.
Ensure electronic donor records are current in the development database, including tracking moves for those within the major gifts portfolio.
Advise and prepare senior leadership for donor meetings as needed.
Manage the strategy and coordination of funder visits with Executive Leadership.
Facilitate connective and grant reporting funder calls as identified.
Lead the planning and management of donor events that combine political education and philanthropic action.

Team Leadership - Manage and evaluate team members and processes for success.

Co-hold the container of the staff team and contractors to support day-to-day development operations and achieve set organizational goals together.
Provide input on development process improvements, and work with teammates to refine collaborative systems as necessary.
Work collaboratively and consistently with other leaders at Essie to define strategic priorities, make decisions about unanticipated opportunities, and manage towards operational plan goals.
Manage departmental budgets and work systems, and co-build and manage a dynamic Communications & Partnerships staff team.
Embody and promote Essie culture and values internally and externally.
Directly manage 1-2 staff members.

Who We’re Looking For

Ideal Qualifications

5+ years of development-related work experience, including experience with individual giving campaigns and direct responsibility for donor relationship development.
Advanced experience managing a staff team and in creating and directing team-wide strategy.
Advanced experience in securing strategic partnership agreements to advance an organization’s mission.
Highly organized with an attention to detail that ensures successful tracking, management, and engaged donor relationships.
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to represent the organization and its work to donors as well as interface with a rich diversity of donors, volunteers, and staff while maintaining tact, diplomacy, and confidentiality.
Impeccable attention to detail and effective writing, editing, and verbal communication skills.
Adept with Mac operating systems, Google Suite, and MS Office Suite (especially Excel, Powerpoint and Word) and donor databases, preferably Salesforce.
Experience supervising people in a way that acknowledges differentials in privilege and power, recognizes their gifts, encourages their confidence, supports their growth, and holds them accountable to standards and achieving collective goals.
Commitment to the beliefs and values of Essie with a demonstrated passion for Black feminism and progressive politics, specifically in gender justice, race justice and ending mass incarceration.

Qualities

A uniquely skilled, empathetic communicator. You are someone who uses your highly developed sense of empathy to tap into what motivates others to act. Because of your belief that everyone benefits from the type of future for which our membership fights, you find ways to make meaningful connections to our work for individuals who may not have had any direct experience with poverty, incarceration, or race, gender, or heteronormative bias.
Immaculately organized in approach. You understand that coordinating multiple projects with complex data necessitates an efficient process. You feel comfortable creating and utilizing project management systems that ensure deadlines and details aren’t missed.
Discernment and honesty we can trust. You are a thoughtful team member who acts in alignment with your integrity and are unfailingly trustworthy. You earn rather than demand the trust of people by listening and making decisions thoughtfully.
Committed to evolution. You are committed to continuously deepening and evolving your own understanding of systems of oppression through study, openness, and humility. And you easily recognize your own relationship to privilege and power, examining and shifting your behaviors as appropriate.
Uplifting and additive. You see mistakes as opportunities for growth, problems as catalysts for solutions, and inspire others along the journey. You carry a positive approach, can-do attitude, and authentic kindness wherever you go.

The Position

The Associate Director of Development is a full-time, salaried, exempt position. This position is supervised by the Interim Co-Executive Director. The salary for this position is between $110k-$120k depending on experience with full medical, dental, and vision benefits, optional 401(k), a substantial vacation package, and a monthly personal wellness stipend. The position is based in one of Essie’s offices in Oakland or Los Angeles, California.

To Apply

Please address a personal, specific, and thoughtful cover letter to the “Essie Hiring Committee” and submit along with a resume through our hiring portal (https://essiejusticegroup.bamboohr.com/jobs). Your resume tells us what you can do; your cover letter should tell us who you are and why you want to work with Essie.

Essie Justice Group provides equal employment and advancement opportunities to all staff members. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and skills. Essie does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, immigration status, socioeconomic status, ancestry, age, size, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, familial status, veteran status, disability, AIDS/HIV status, medical condition, prior conviction, arrest history, traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Essie values and specifically seeks applicants who are people with incarcerated loved ones; formerly incarcerated people; people of color; women; queer, transgender, gender expansive, and gender fluid people.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, performance assessment, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

About Essie Justice Group

Essie Justice Group is a non profit organization of women with incarcerated loved ones taking on the rampant injustices created by mass incarceration. Our award-winning Healing to Advocacy Model brings women together to heal, build collective power, and drive social change. Essie is

Great Place to Work-Certified™ by Great Place to Work.

Learn more at www.essiejusticegroup.org.

new_jobs.title: Deputy Director Public Works
new_jobs.description:
Description

If you want to join a hardworking team that shares a commitment to providing top-quality municipal services in a prime Northern California location, consider a career with the City of Arcata and apply today!
We are currently recruiting for the position of Deputy Director Public Works.

Please note:
Interviews are tentatively scheduled for Thursday, September 24th. Please hold this date.

Enjoy GREAT BENEFITS including: the City currently pays the majority of the medical coverage premium for employees (and their dependents) and 100% of the premium for dental and vision coverage. If applicable, the City also offers a $400/month health insurance opt-out option. Additionally, the City offers this position 14 days of Management Leave annually; vacation accrual increases with service; immediate City contribution to deferred compensation, increasing with service; longevity pay, etc. See more in the "Benefits" tab.

Description

Under general direction of the Director of Public Works, this position plans, organizes, coordinates, manages, and supervises assigned personnel, programs, operations, and activities within the Streets, Water Distribution, Wastewater Collections, and Central Garage Divisions of the Public Works Department; provides highly complex and responsible support to the Public Works Director in areas of expertise; and performs all other related duties as assigned.

An ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced, multi-priority environment; demonstrates high emotional intelligence; is established as a motivating and supportive leader; and successfully collaborates across internal departments and with outside agency partners.

Also note:
With an upcoming City reorganization and the creation of a Public Works Department in process, the position title and job description have been updated accordingly. We anticipate the reorganization process to be completed by January 1, 2027 with more information available regarding the Department structure.

Examples of Duties

Manages and participates in the development and implementation of goals, objectives, policies and priorities for assigned Divisions; develops and standardizes procedures and methods to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of Division programs and activities; continuously monitors and evaluates the efficiency and effectiveness of service delivery methods and procedures; identifies opportunities for improvement and provides recommendation to the Director.
Plans, manages, and oversees the daily functions, operations, and activities of the Streets/Utilities Divisions, including construction, operation and maintenance of streets, water distribution system, wastewater collection system, and central garage; manages and coordinates the work plan for the assigned Divisions; assesses and monitors workload, administrative and support systems, and internal reporting relationships; meets with staff to identify and resolve problems; assigns work activities, projects and programs; monitors workflow; reviews and evaluates work products, methods and procedures.
Serves as the City’s Legally Responsible Officer (i.e. LRO) for the City’s water distribution and wastewater collection systems; including obtaining and maintaining Water Distribution Operator and Wastewater Collection System Maintenance certificates at least at the level required by the state based on the state’s designation of the grade of distribution and collection systems; higher certificate levels may be required as determined necessary by the City.
Manages project coordination for assigned construction or capital improvement projects, including planning, budgeting/finance development, design and development of project specifications, review, construction and inspection processes; requests, evaluates, negotiates and manages consultant proposals and contracts; assists in identification of and securing financing options for projects; sets project schedules, design review elements, agency coordination, regulatory agency compliance, and budgeting consideration in accordance with appropriate standards.
Oversees, manages, and directs the work of outside consultants and contractors, observing all applicable City administrative policies and procedures; reviews and evaluates work products and/or services for compliance with the City’s objectives, quality, and contract scope; approves payment of invoices for contractual work as appropriate.
Develops and maintains standard operating procedures, division safety programs and division emergency response program, including providing training to staff on applicable local, state, and federal policies and practices; providing required certification programs; instructs and provides training for staff in work methods, use of equipment and relevant safety precautions.
Participates in the selection, trains, motivates, and evaluates assigned personnel; provides or coordinates staff training; works with employees to correct deficiencies; implements discipline and termination procedures.
Manages and participates in the development, administration and monitoring of assigned Division budgets and applicable Capital Improvement Plans.
Responds to inquiries, requests, and complaints as it relates to division and department functions and takes appropriate action; ensures the public is kept updated and aware of programs, projects, and other related activities through the department’s public notification policies and procedures.
Leads the Department’s asset management program to identify, assess condition of, and prioritize improvements for streets and underground utility infrastructure by utilizing the Department’s asset management software and geographic information system.
Performs the duties of Director, as assigned, during their absence.
Performs all other related duties as assigned.

See job description for full list of duties.

Typical Qualifications And Requirements

Knowledge of:
Principles, practices, regulations and techniques related to the construction, operations and management of Streets, Water Distribution, Wastewater Collections, and Central Garage; principles and practices of personnel and program management, including goal setting, program development, implementation, evaluation, and project management; supervision, training, evaluating, and disciplining of staff, either directly or through subordinate levels of supervision; principles and practices of public sector budget development and administration; applicable Federal, State, and local laws, codes and regulations concerning the operation of Streets, Water Distribution, Wastewater Collections, and Central Garage Divisions; principles and techniques of capital improvement design, funding and long-term maintenance; principles and practices of contract administration, including public bidding requirements; report writing principles and practices; business mathematics; standard office computer software, including word processing, spreadsheets, database and electronic reporting programs; English usage, grammar, spelling, vocabulary, and punctuation; techniques for dealing effectively with those contacted in the course of work, in person, electronically and on the telephone.

Ability to:
Read, analyze, understand and apply a wide variety of laws, rules and regulations, instruction manuals, plans and profiles, diagrams, labels, and other technical information; develop and maintain records management systems in accordance with legal requirements; interpret, explain, and ensure compliance with City policies and procedures, complex laws, codes, regulations and ordinances; evaluate and develop improvements in operations, procedures, policies, or methods; research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery methods, procedures and techniques; analyze, interpret, summarize and present administrative and technical information and data in an effective manner; plan, organize, schedule, assign, review and evaluate the work of staff; prepare and administer assigned budgets; prepare clear and concise reports, correspondence, policies, procedures and other written materials; conduct complex research projects, evaluate alternatives, make sound recommendations; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; operate a computer, electronic devices, and necessary software applications, and other applicable standard office equipment; establish and maintain effective and cooperative working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.

Additional Information

Other Requirements

Possess a Valid California Class C Driver’s License.
Possess a State of California Water Distribution Operator Grade 1 certificate.
Obtain a Grade 3 State of California Water Distribution Operator Certificate within eighteen (18) months of hire, or Certificate Grade required by the state to serve as the Legally Responsible Officer (i.e. LRO) for the Water Distribution System.
Obtain a Grade 2 State of California Wastewater Collection System Maintenance Certificate within eighteen (18) months of hire, or Certificate Grade required by the State.
Other certificate(s) specific to functional area of assignment may be required.
A commitment to support inclusion in the workplace.
Willing and available to respond as needed outside of normal work hours, including being available by cellular phone and/or other communication devices.
Willing and available to attend meetings after normal work hours; to travel for trainings and/or meetings; and to work extended hours, nights and/or weekends as necessary to complete assigned tasks, including responding to emergency calls.
Ability to respond in person to an emergency in the City within thirty (30) minutes.

Physical Requirements

Work is performed in a general office and field environment. Must be able to perform the physical aspects of the job, including sitting and standing for periods of time, operating standard office equipment, including a computer; visit various City sites, including traversing uneven terrain; climbing ladders, crawling in confined areas, bending and stooping; operating a motor vehicle; hearing and speech to communicate in person and over the telephone; lift, push, pull, and carry up to 50 lbs.; work around and come in contact with raw sewage, hazardous/toxic chemicals, strong odors, and infectious disease; occasionally working outside in varying weather conditions, with occasional exposure to dust, pollen and heavy equipment.

Experience And Training

Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be:

Equivalent to a Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, or related field, and at least five (5) years progressively responsible experience in public infrastructure development and maintenance activities or related service delivery operations, including at least three (3) years related supervisory and budgetary experience.
Additional related experience at the supervisor and/or management level can be substituted for the education requirement on a year by year basis.

DISASTER SERVICE WORKER

All City of Arcata employees are designated Disaster Service Workers through state and local law (California Government Code Section 3100-3109). Employment with the City requires the affirmation of a loyalty oath to this effect. Employees are required to complete all Disaster Service Worker related training as assigned and to return to work as ordered in the event of an emergency.

Job Summary

The Executive Director serves as the University’s senior event leader, providing strategic direction, institutional governance, and executive oversight for all presidential-level and other high-impact University events, including commencement ceremonies and other major institutional events. Reporting to and closely aligned with the Vice President, Chief of Staff, and University Secretary, in the Office of the President, this role is responsible for setting vision, priorities, and standards for the University’s event portfolio while ensuring consistent, high-quality execution and protection of the University’s reputation.

This position provides strong executive leadership over the event team, with a clear expectation of effective delegation, performance management, and accountability across all assigned staff and event portfolios. The Executive Director is ultimately accountable for outcomes, but achieves results by building capacity within the team, empowering leaders at all levels, and ensuring decisions are made at the appropriate level, rather than through personal control of day-to-day tactics.

As the strategic lead for university events, the Executive Director operates at the portfolio and enterprise level, translating presidential and University priorities into cohesive event strategies, setting standards and protocols, managing risk, and guiding teams to deliver results within defined frameworks. This role requires the ability to move fluidly between strategy and execution, stepping in directly where necessary for the most sensitive or high-stakes events, while maintaining focus on long-term planning, organizational effectiveness, and continuous improvement.

The Executive Director leads cross-functional collaboration with academic and administrative partners, exercises sound financial oversight of event budgets and resources, and serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership. A core responsibility of the role is ensuring that institutional protocol, quality control, and risk assessment are embedded into all planning and execution, and that leaders are equipped with clear, timely, and decision-ready information.

This position reflects a deliberate shift toward a tiered, standards-driven, governance-oriented, and data-informed model for managing University events. In its early phases, the Executive Director is responsible for building and operationalizing the governance framework, establishing clear roles, decision rights, and performance expectations, and strengthening the Office’s capacity to operate effectively without over-reliance on any single individual. The role is expected to lead at a strategic and enterprise level, setting direction, priorities, and standards; developing leaders within the team; and ensuring accountability for results. Execution is intentionally focused on institutional-level and high-stakes events, with the Executive Director engaging directly where executive judgment, visibility, or risk requires it, while otherwise ensuring work is appropriately delegated and managed. Central to this work is improving efficiency, enforcing portfolio discipline, and implementing meaningful measures of success to guide future investment, resource allocation, and decision-making.

While ultimately accountable for outcomes, the Executive Director is expected to delegate execution responsibility to portfolio-owning leaders, intervening directly only when institutional risk, protocol exception, or executive visibility requires.

Collaborate with the Vice President, Chief of Staff, and University Secretary to translate University and presidential priorities into a cohesive, intentional event portfolio.
Build a high-functioning leadership team and operational structure that enables the Office to perform effectively without over-reliance on the Executive Director for day-to-day tactical decision-making.
Provide direct leadership and oversight of all professionals within the Office.
Ensure teams are on track with planning, execution, timelines, and deliverables across all assigned event portfolios.
Set and enforce event priorities, sequencing, and scope decisions to balance institutional risk, capacity, and strategic value.
Coach, guide, and hold staff accountable for performance, quality, and adherence to institutional standards.

Job Summary

The Senior Director of Development, Divisions and Institutes will be responsible for major gift fundraising for university-wide initiatives, including Divisions, Institutes and non-academic departments, as determined by the Senior Vice President of Institutional Advancement. Primary responsibilities include developing and managing a portfolio of approximately 150 prospects/suspects, including alumni and friends of the University, and seeking, soliciting, and securing major gifts of $25,000 and above to the University.

Job Responsibilities

Manage a portfolio of approximately 150 prospects in support of the designated division, institute, and/or unit
Develop and implement strategies for the cultivation, engagement, solicitation, and stewardship of major gift ($25,000 and above) prospects.
Determine donor interest and develop and execute an individualized plan for each prospect. Solicit every prospect for an annual gift during each fiscal year, in addition to major and planned gifts as appropriate.
Recommend suitable giving opportunities and prepare major gift proposals for specific initiatives and priorities.
Participate in and advise on strategies that contribute to the development of a strong prospect pipeline.
Work with other members of the Advancement team to appropriately engage assigned prospects in University activities.
Participate as an active member of the prospect management process, including and especially identifying new prospects and developing strategies for those prospects.
Actively engage with assigned prospects to follow up on, and secure pledge payments in a timely manner to support pledge fulfillment efforts.
Ensure gift recognition occurs and acknowledgements are sent from the appropriate individuals in Advancement.
Partner with division and institute leadership to identify funding priorities, translate programmatic needs into compelling cases for support, and align development efforts with strategic goals.
Lead complex gift negotiations and close gifts that advance institutional priorities.
Provide leadership and mentorship to development staff supporting divisions and institutes, as applicable.
Partner with colleagues across development (annual giving, prospect research, donor relations, etc.) to maximize fundraising outcomes.
Represent St. John’s University externally with donors, partners, and community stakeholders.
Utilize data, analytics, and donor insights to inform strategy and optimize performance.
Play a leadership role in capital campaigns and strategic initiatives tied to divisions and institutes.
Contribute to messaging, case development, and donor engagement strategies.
Collaborate on cross-functional initiatives that span multiple areas of the organization.

Supervisory Responsibility

Manage one Assistant Director of Development

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time, with or without notice.

Competencies, Education, Experience

Leadership & Professional Excellence: Demonstrated strength in leadership, project management, collaboration, analytical thinking, and stakeholder engagement.
Relationship Building & Agility: Skilled at building strong relationships in donor-facing and professional settings; comfortable operating in social environments. Ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt quickly in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
Communication & Organization: Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with strong organizational ability and attention to detail.
Problem Solving & Judgment: Proven ability to think critically, resolve complex issues, work independently, and exercise sound professional judgment.
Technical Proficiency: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), including presentations, reporting, and data analysis.
CRM & Development Systems Expertise: Experience with fundraising and CRM platforms such as Ellucian (Advance/Banner), Salesforce (Affinaquest, Ascend), or Blackbaud (CRM, Raiser’s Edge, NXT), with a focus on prospect management and pipeline tracking.

Required Education And Experience

Bachelor’s Degree required.
Minimum of 8–12 years of progressive experience in fundraising, advancement, or a related field.
Minimum of 7+ years of one-on-one leadership ($1,500+) and/or major gift ($25,000+) solicitation experience.
Minimum of 7+ years’ experience in Development, preferably in a Higher Education environment.
Proven ability to build and manage relationships with senior leaders, donors, and external stakeholders.
Demonstrated knowledge of development practices and principles and a track record of success in managing leadership or major gift prospects and in securing gifts.
Demonstrated skill to work within a complex environment with strong capabilities in planning, organizing, and managing.
Ability to work collaboratively with colleagues and peers in the Advancement area and with internal partners and external volunteers.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Demonstrated interpersonal skills.
Flexibility to travel, largely on a local/regional basis. Occasional weekend and evening work will be necessary, as well as occasional travel nationally.
Affinity and commitment to the mission of St. John’s University.

Preferred Education & Experience

Advanced degree (e.g., Master’s, MBA, or relevant field) preferred.
Experience in complex, matrixed organizations such as healthcare systems, higher education, research institutions, or large nonprofit environments.
Experience supporting or leading capital campaigns or large-scale fundraising initiatives.
Familiarity with donor databases/CRMs and pipeline management tools.
Experience working with faculty, or academic/institute program leadership.

Supplemental Information

Work Environment

Working in the University Center, where Advancement is housed, as well as off campus, to visit with donors and prospects. Primary equipment includes the phone, laptop computer, and commercial printers.

Physical Demands

Prolonged periods of sitting and working at a computer, including virtual meetings and document preparation.

Frequent verbal communication in person, over the phone, and via virtual platforms.

Ability to travel regularly, including local and regional travel and occasional national travel; may involve extended periods of sitting, standing, or walking.

Ability to attend and actively participate in events, which may require standing for extended periods.

Occasional lifting and carrying of materials related to events or meetings (typically up to 10–15 pounds).

Environmental Conditions

Primarily office-based with a hybrid work environment (as applicable).

Frequent attendance at events outside of standard business hours (evenings and weekends) to support donor engagement and stewardship.

Work is fast-paced and deadline-driven, requiring the ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing needs.

Prolonged periods of sitting, working at a computer, and participating in virtual and in-person meetings.

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work

Full-time position with office hours matching University business day as well as off hours, attending events on nights and weekends as needed. Expectations are for flexibility as needed for events and fundraising opportunities outside of those hours.

Travel

There may be some travel involved, since the assigned prospects may not be local. Having a car is necessary for this position.

Along with exceptional benefits such as medical, dental, life insurance, long term disability insurance, tuition remission, generous 403(b) employer contribution, employee assistance program, and liberal paid time off policies, faculty and staff can also enjoy St. John’s performing arts, libraries, bookstores, dining facilities, campus recreation and sporting events

new_jobs.title: Deputy Director of Rutgers Brain Health Institute
new_jobs.description:
Posting Summary

The Rutgers Brain Health Institute ( BHI ) serves as the umbrella neuroscience organization across Rutgers University, encompassing over 300 research laboratories and 900 trainees. Members include faculty from 50 departments and 14 schools at Rutgers. This represents one of the largest concentrations of neuroscience- and brain health-related research talent in the world. Our work is organized into four key focus areas: neurodevelopment, neurodegeneration, motivational and affective neuroscience, and cognitive and sensory neuroscience. Since our inception in 2014, BHI has experienced tremendous growth. We have successfully recruited over 48 tenure-track faculty members, with more on the way, and established five Centers of Research Excellence. These include centers dedicated to addiction research, autism research, Alzheimer’s disease research, human neuroimaging, and computational cognitive neuropsychiatry. Additional centers in pain research and neurotechnology are being developed. We seek an accomplished scientist, at the Professor or Associate Professor level, to join the BHI as its new Deputy Director. The deputy director will play a key role in helping to develop and execute the vision and mission of BHI in addition to leading an active federally funded research program in their area of research interest. The Deputy Director will be responsible for leading the implementation of the BHI Strategic Plan , as well as revising and developing new plan goals. In addition, the Deputy Director will lead BHI efforts to develop research training and mentoring programs for physician-researchers. The Deputy Director will also help recruit and retain physician-researchers in neuroscience and brain health research. The ideal candidate will be a leader in a research area within neuroscience or brain health research with a strong, federally funded research program, who can leverage, stimulate, and lead translational science approaches from basic science to clinical to population levels. We seek candidates who have a broad understanding and vision of translational neuroscience and strongly believe in advancing brain health through cutting-edge interdisciplinary research. The ideal candidate will also need to be comfortable with a forward-facing role, consistent with the high profile this role will hold at Rutgers and within New Jersey. Physician-researchers are especially encouraged to apply. With two teaching hospitals and neuroscience labs in Newark and New Brunswick/Piscataway, an affiliation with the largest and most accomplished health systems in the state ( RWJBH ), as well as proximity to the New York, Princeton and Philadelphia neuroscience communities, Rutgers BHI offers tremendous collaborative opportunities and core facilities to support and grow outstanding research programs. The successful candidate will be a visionary leader who can foster collaborations among existing research and training programs, develop new research opportunities based on relevant federal, state and industry priorities, and actively engage in BHI philanthropic initiatives. Applicants must have an MD/PhD, MD, or PhD, with demonstrated ability to lead an independent NIH -funded research program. Prior leadership and administrative experience in academia will be important. We offer substantial resources to support the deputy director’s research activities, as well as activities across BHI . With a NIH CTSA , Rutgers also offers unique opportunities to speed the translation of research discoveries into clinical trials and improved patient care. Outstanding core facilities will support this position. Rutgers values a culturally diverse faculty; we strongly encourage applications from female and candidates underrepresented in medicine. Applicants should submit a CV and statement of research accomplishments and vision to Dr. Carlos Pato, the Chair of the search committee, at bhi@bhi.rutgers.edu .

Chief Executive Officer (CEO)

Lead an Organization Devoted to the Strength of Family

The Family Initiative, Inc. (TFI) is seeking an accomplished and visionary leader to serve as its next Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
. This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a mission-driven organization dedicated to strengthening children, families, and communities through innovative services, advocacy, and operational excellence.

The CEO serves as the chief executive and strategic leader of The Family Initiative, Inc. and its affiliated organizations, guiding a multi-state enterprise that delivers child welfare, behavioral health, family support, technology, and nonprofit support services. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CEO is responsible for advancing the organization's mission, ensuring financial sustainability, fostering organizational excellence, and positioning TFI for continued growth and impact.

The Family Initiative, Inc. is the parent organization providing services to children and families across the United States through its affiliates:

TFI Family Services (Kansas, Nebraska, and Missouri)
TFI Family Connections (Oklahoma)
Texas Family Initiative (Texas)
Pathway Family Services (Kansas and Texas)
Mainstream Nonprofit Solutions, providing shared services and nonprofit support
Foster Care Technologies, delivering technology solutions for child welfare organizations

TFI is a private, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization governed by a voluntary Board of Directors committed to strengthening families and improving outcomes for children and communities.

Position Summary

The Chief Executive Officer provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for the TFI Family of Companies. The CEO partners closely with the Board of Directors to establish organizational priorities, guide long-term planning, ensure financial stewardship, and advance the mission and vision of the organization.

This leader will oversee a complex and growing enterprise, ensuring high-quality service delivery, regulatory compliance, organizational stability, and strong relationships with community partners, funders, government agencies, and other key stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Develop and execute long-term strategic plans in partnership with the Board of Directors.
Establish organizational goals, priorities, and policies that support mission achievement and sustainable growth.
Lead organizational innovation and identify opportunities for expansion and service enhancement.
Guide strategic initiatives, partnerships, mergers, acquisitions, or other growth opportunities.

Board Partnership and Governance

Serve as Chair of the Executive Team and an ex-officio member of all Board committees.
Support the Board's governance responsibilities through timely communication, planning, and policy recommendations.
Advise the Board on strategic, operational, financial, and regulatory matters.

Operational Excellence

Ensure effective administration of programs, services, and organizational operations.
Monitor organizational performance and implement corrective actions when necessary.
Promote efficiency, accountability, continuous improvement, and organizational effectiveness.

Financial Stewardship

Provide oversight of budgeting, financial planning, and fiscal management.
Ensure the long-term financial health and sustainability of the organization.
Monitor financial performance and maintain strong internal controls and risk management practices.

External Relations and Advocacy

Serve as the primary spokesperson and ambassador for the organization.
Build and maintain strong relationships with government agencies, community partners, legislators, funders, and stakeholders.
Represent the organization in public forums, legislative matters, community events, and media engagements.

Organizational Culture and Talent Leadership

Foster a culture grounded in TFI's mission, vision, and values.
Recruit, develop, and retain high-performing leaders and teams.
Champion diversity, inclusion, collaboration, and professional development throughout the organization.

Compliance and Risk Management

Ensure compliance with applicable local, state, and federal laws and regulations.
Maintain effective policies, procedures, and systems of organizational accountability.
Oversee organizational risk management efforts and ensure operational integrity.

Qualifications/Required Qualifications

Master's degree in social work, business administration, public administration, or a related field is required
Minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience within child welfare, behavioral health, human services, or related fields.
Senior executive leadership experience with responsibility for organizational strategy, operations, and financial oversight.
Demonstrated success in financial management, including budgeting, fiscal planning, and stewardship of organizational resources.
Experience working effectively with Boards of Directors, government agencies, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Experience managing government-funded programs.

Preferred Qualifications

Multi-state organizational leadership experience.
Experience leading multi-entity or complex organizational structures.
Experience operating in one or more TFI service states.
Experience within a Community-Based Care (CBC), Single Source Continuum Contractor (SSCC), or similar service delivery model.
Demonstrated success leading organizational growth, transformation, or expansion initiatives.

The Ideal Candidate

The Successful Candidate Will Demonstrate

Strategic Thinking

The ability to navigate complexity, evaluate data and financial information, anticipate challenges, and establish a clear direction for the future.

Operational Agility

A disciplined and adaptable leader who can execute strategy, ensure compliance, and respond effectively to changing environments.

Interpersonal Savvy

A relationship-focused executive who builds trust, communicates effectively, negotiates skillfully, and inspires confidence.

People Leadership

A leader who develops others, cultivates talent, and fosters alignment around a shared mission and vision.

Travel Requirements

This position requires significant travel, including regional and overnight travel, to organizational locations, Board meetings, community events, legislative functions, and stakeholder engagements.

Compensation is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience.

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Retirement benefits
Paid time off
Employee assistance programs
Professional development opportunities
Additional employee benefits and wellness resources

Qualified candidates are encouraged to submit a resume and cover letter through TFI's online employment application system. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

seeks an Executive Director who is responsible for carrying out all programs and advocacy activities that advance the mission of the CLS under direction from the Board of Advisors and consistent with the needs and support of CLS member organizations. Legislative Advocacy and Communications

The CLS is recognized as a trusted, responsive resource for members of Congress, congressional staff, and Administration officials on NIH, NSF, and other federal agency life-sciences research policy
The CLS identifies and responds early to federal legislative and policy developments affecting NIH, NSF, and other federal agencies that fund, regulate, or enable life-sciences research
The Board of Advisors has clear, expert-informed advocacy priorities and messaging that responds to the federal policy environment and aligns with the CLS mission and member interests
A strong and engaged grass tops network mobilizes the life-sciences community to support CLS advocacy objectives through timely, coordinated outreach to policymakers
The CLS digital and direct communications consistently inform, engage, and activate target audiences, strengthening the organization’s visibility, policy influence, and member connection

CLS Programs

Successful Congressional Biomedical Research Briefings measured by the delivery of relevant programs developed collaboratively with event co-chairs and seamless execution of all logistics
A successful annual Congressional Life Science Fair measured by the execution of a well-developed event plan/program, attendance, event marketing, and seamless execution of logistics
Delivery of high-quality presentations and seamless execution of all necessary logistics to support all other external events in which CLS engages

Financial Sustainability

A budget aligned to CLS strategy and priorities is developed annually in partnership with the CLS Board Chair, the ASCB CEO and the ASCB COFO, and subsequently board approved

The Board of Advisors and the Congressional Liaison Committee have well-planned, productive, and decision-ready meetings (video and in-person) supported by timely agendas, schedules, and high-quality briefing materials

Additional Activities

Effective relationships are maintained with all member organizations to ensure their continued engagement and financial support for CLS

Other duties as determined/assigned to support advancing the work of CLS

Candidate Background

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in public policy, biological sciences or related field or equivalent experience;
Master’s or higher a plus

8+ years of experience working with/in the federal science policy landscape

Proven experience on Capitol Hill, with established relationships and a strong network of contacts
among congressional offices, committees, and other relevant federal policymakers

Strong program development/management and fundraising expertise

Established track record in budget development and financial/resource management

Knowledge and Skills

Outstanding interpersonal skills, with a high degree of patience and tact. Must be able to cultivate respectful, strategic, collaborative and influential relationships with individuals from diverse backgrounds
Political savvy to quickly react to critical issues
Well-versed on policy issues related to life science and science funding
Excellent written and oral communication skills
Works well under pressure and on tight deadlines
Demonstrates an interest in the mission of the CLS and the ability to communicate the value proposition of CLS to our partners and collaborators
Able to work across multiple digital platforms and adaptable to new technology and systems

This position is primarily remote, but a physical presence in the ASCB Headquarters office in Rockville, MD is required a minimum of once every two weeks

new_jobs.title: Branch Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
As a thought-leader and best-in-class provider in education, wellness, youth development, and community-building, The YMCA of Metro Atlanta is one of the oldest and most essential non-profits serving in Atlanta. Today, we’re looking for you to join us as we carry out our mission to positively impact lives and communities across the state.

At the Y, we’re an association of like-minded people (staff, volunteers, and members), on the forefront of a movement to ensure that everyone -- especially children -- experience an equal opportunity to reach their full potential. In the course of a year, we provide more than 3,000 children, ages 6 weeks through Pre-K with high-quality literacy and STEAM-infused learning; give 58,000 youth and teens access to sports, aquatics, day and resident camps, teen leadership development programs, and employment opportunities; provide over 200,000 members with programs, services, and facilities to enjoy connection and maintain wellness regardless of age; and engage over 25,000 volunteers and donors from across Atlanta to share in the gift of supporting their communities.

Nature And Scope

The YMCA of Metro Atlanta is seeking a passionate and forward-thinking executive director with a proven, successful track record of developing a strong branch board, increasing annual giving, engaging community through increasing membership and programs while advancing the Y’s impact in the community.

This highly motivated leader who is impact focused and entrepreneurial by nature will report directly to the Group Vice President and will have primary responsibility for day-to-day operations. Experience in and a demonstrated track record of the areas of staff supervision, membership and program development, fiscal management, fundraising, volunteer cultivation, and community engagement are required. The continued development and coaching of an experienced staff team to new levels of service will be key to achieving full potential.

RESPONSIBILITIES (including, But Not Limited To)

Establish a culture of quality and service to meet and exceed the goals and objectives set forth in the strategic plan and standards established by the Board of Directors.
Represents and promotes the Y in the local community by developing strategic, positive working and collaborative relationships with other organizations, businesses, and governmental entities.
Develop, manage, and monitor a balanced operating budget to meet or exceed budgeted targets.
Develop and direct high quality, relationship-based member engagement strategies.
Provide metrics to measure program/membership impact, staff, and program and membership satisfaction.
Maintain branch and association certifications in CPR, Multimedia First Aid, Blood-borne Pathogens, Metro Atlanta YMCA new staff orientation, branch orientation and branch emergency procedures.
Manage delivery of related programs to exceed YMCA standards and program objectives.
Participate in branch and Association-wide activities and initiatives.
Act as the LEAD campaigner for Why It Matters Annual Giving Campaign including but not limited to volunteer recruitment, training and support, and lead as an integral member of the management team committed to reaching stated fund-raising goals.
Serve on the Executive Cabinet, liaison with appropriate professional groups in the community and serve on Metro Task Forces.
Effective board development including recruitment of board members who represent the branch community and developing a strong board committee structure.
Ensures revenue growth through a climate of innovation to develop member-focused programs which support the Y mission, goals, and strategies.
Effectively mentor, supervise, and develop branch staff and volunteers and build an exceptional culture to motivate them to achieve their personal and professional goals.
Responsible for facility management and maintenance to ensure high quality facilities, grounds, and equipment. A culture of risk management and safety is maintained at the branch. Maintains required safety and training certifications, Emergency Action Plans, SDS Manuals, etc.

Requirements

Bachelor's Degree and 8+ years overall leadership experience or high school diploma and 12+ years of directly relevant experience with the Y or closely related non-profit
2+ years of successful experience managing large teams in an executive level/senior management position
Business management skills and demonstrated ability to lead people
Proven ability to establish and maintain collaborations with community organization, corporations, and government agencies
Strong attention to detail
Passionate commitment to the YMCA mission, values, and purpose
CPR and First Aid certifications required within 30 days of hire

Preferred Requirements

Bachelor's degree in human services, social services, business or equivalent
Experience in directing total operations through volunteer development, supervision of staff, development and monitoring of branch budget, marketing and public relations, and program development
Hands on experience working with a diverse population in a YMCA strongly preferred
12+ years of directly relevant experience with the YMCA or closely related non-profit
4+ years of management experience, strategic vision and relationship building preferably in a YMCA or other nonprofit agency

Employment and Benefits package for this job posting is offered through the YMCA of Metropolitan Atlanta, Inc.

Employment Requirement

Ability to pass a pre-employment background check including Criminal Record check, Drug Screening, motor vehicle record (MVR) and reference check according to company policy.
Must be legally eligible to work in the US without current or future sponsorship.

This job posting is subject to change at any time.

The YMCA of Metropolitan Atlanta offers excellent benefits and career opportunities as part of our culture of excellence. The opportunities to serve are vast, and we’re looking for like minded people, who share our values of CARING, HONESTY, RESPECT, and RESPONSIBILITY to join us and do their best work.

The YMCA of Metropolitan Atlanta does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected by law.

new_jobs.description:
Managing Director, Philanthropy & External Affairs

Location:
Hybrid | Boston, MA preferred

Salary:
$120,000–$140,000, commensurate with experience

About Kids In Tech

Kids in Tech equips young people with the skills and confidence to succeed in a technology-driven world through hands-on STEAM programming.

We are entering a significant growth phase, including the launch of a public-facing STEM Innovation Lab in Boston's Seaport, alongside a broader strategy for program expansion, organizational growth, and long-term sustainability.

The Opportunity

Kids in Tech is seeking a Managing Director, Philanthropy & External Affairs to lead philanthropic revenue growth and external positioning for the organization.

Working closely with the CEO, this leader will build and execute a diversified philanthropic strategy, cultivate and secure major and transformational gifts, expand corporate and foundation partnerships, and help shape and execute a significant multi-year comprehensive campaign supporting Kids in Tech's next phase of growth.

This is a senior, externally facing leadership role for a builder who can develop strategy, cultivate relationships, create a strong fundraising pipeline, and close significant funding.

What You'll Lead

Philanthropy & Revenue Growth

Develop and lead a diversified philanthropic revenue strategy across major and individual giving, foundations, corporate philanthropy, and other private philanthropic sources.
Build and manage a strong fundraising pipeline with clear targets and accountability.
Personally cultivate, solicit, and secure significant gifts and strategic investments.
Establish revenue goals, forecasts, pipeline targets, and performance benchmarks in partnership with the CEO.

Comprehensive Campaign

Partner with the CEO and campaign advisors to assess campaign readiness and establish an ambitious, evidence-based campaign goal.
Develop campaign strategy, donor segmentation, cultivation pathways, prospect strategies, and measurable fundraising targets.
Develop compelling campaign materials and cases for investment.
Help activate the Board of Directors in prospect identification, introductions, cultivation, solicitation, and campaign activity.

Partnerships & External Relations

Build high-value relationships across corporate, philanthropic, civic, and education sectors.
Represent Kids in Tech at events, convenings, and stakeholder meetings.
Strengthen the organization's visibility and positioning across Boston and beyond.

Donor Strategy & Fundraising Infrastructure

Build a disciplined prospect identification and research function.
Develop donor stewardship and engagement strategies that strengthen retention and create pathways to increased giving.
Build strong fundraising systems, including CRM practices, moves management, pipeline reporting, forecasting, and stewardship tracking.
Maximize the CEO's fundraising engagement through prospect strategy, briefing materials, asks, and follow-up.

External Communications & Brand

Lead external communications, storytelling, marketing, and brand positioning.
Translate program outcomes and organizational impact into compelling donor, partner, and public-facing narratives.
Oversee donor and stakeholder communications, including impact reports, newsletters, campaign communications, and stewardship materials.

Team Leadership

Build and lead the development and external relations function as Kids in Tech grows.
Establish clear KPIs, reporting systems, and accountability structures.
Define the team structure and hiring roadmap needed to scale the function.

You Might Be a Great Fit If You...

Have personally cultivated, solicited, and closed significant gifts or funding commitments.
Have built or substantially expanded a fundraising pipeline rather than solely managed an established portfolio.
Have experience leading or playing a significant role in a comprehensive, capital, or major growth campaign.
Are comfortable engaging senior executives, major donors, funders, civic leaders, and other external stakeholders.
Can translate mission and impact into compelling funding opportunities.
Have built or scaled a development, philanthropy, or partnerships function.
Thrive in fast-moving, high-growth environments.
Combine strategic thinking with strong execution and follow-through.

We welcome candidates whose fundraising experience comes from nonprofit philanthropy, political campaigns, higher education, healthcare, advocacy, or other relationship-driven fundraising environments.

This Is a Builder Role

This is not a fundraising coordination or support position. The Managing Director will have meaningful ownership and accountability for philanthropic revenue growth and must bring demonstrated experience building relationships, developing pipelines, securing funding, and translating strategy into measurable results.

Compensation & Benefits

Salary: $120,000–$140,000
Health, dental, and vision benefits
Generous PTO
Hybrid flexibility

Equal Opportunity

Kids in Tech is an equal opportunity employer. We strongly encourage applications from individuals from underrepresented backgrounds.

Cover letter prompt

Role

Please submit a cover letter (approximately 1–2 pages) explaining your interest in Kids in Tech and this role. Rather than restating your résumé, please address the following:

Fundraising results: Describe one or two significant gifts, grants, or funding commitments that you personally played a leading role in cultivating, soliciting, and closing. Please include the approximate amount, type of funder, your specific role, and how you moved the opportunity from prospect to commitment.
Building a philanthropic pipeline: Share an example of a fundraising pipeline or development function that you built or substantially expanded. What did you inherit, what did you change, and what measurable results followed?
Campaign experience: Describe your experience with a comprehensive, capital, or major growth campaign. What was the campaign goal, what did you personally own, and what were the results?
Kids in Tech: Based on what you understand about Kids in Tech and our next phase of growth, what excites you about the opportunity to build our philanthropic and external affairs function?

Job Description

The Nebraska Ethanol Board is currently seeking applicants for the Executive Director position within their agency. This is a full-time, exempt position. The executive director serves at the pleasure of the Nebraska Ethanol Board.

In 1971, the Nebraska Legislature created the Agricultural Products Industrial Utilization Committee —now named the Nebraska Ethanol Board— the first state agency in the U.S. devoted solely to the development of the ethanol industry. Today, the Nebraska Ethanol Board continues its mission to support ethanol production and use in Nebraska, serving as a primary resource for ethanol producers, developers, media, regulators and policymakers.

The executive director reports to the board and is responsible for a wide variety of functions including the day-to-day management of the office. Primary responsibilities include but are not limited to: administration of programs and initiatives that support the board’s mission, overall budget development, facilitating agency strategic planning, industry advocacy and development of public policy, business recruitment, and fostering positive relationships with stakeholders and constituents.

new_jobs.description:
Description

The University Librarian & Executive Director of Library Services serves as the chief administrator and strategic leader of the Felix G. Woodward Library at Austin Peay State University. Reporting to the Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs, the University Librarian & Executive Director serves as a member of the Provost’s Leadership Team and provides visionary, collaborative, and innovative leadership for the University’s library services, resources, personnel, facilities, technologies, and learning environments.

The University Librarian & Executive Director is responsible for leading an experienced team of over 25 library faculty and staff; managing the overall library budget of ~3.3M; and planning, implementing, assessing, and continuously improving library programs, collections, services, technologies, and spaces. The position provides visionary leadership for key service areas, including access and discovery, collections and resource management, library technology and digital services, research and instruction, and University archives and special collections.

The University Librarian & Executive Director represents Woodward Library across the University, within the Association of College and Research Libraries (ACRL), and throughout the local and regional community. This position is expected to position the library as a dynamic academic hub that advances APSU’s mission, supports student success, strengthens faculty research and scholarship, promotes equitable access to information, and contributes meaningfully to the intellectual and cultural life of the University.

Primary Duties And Responsibilities

Provide strategic, forward-thinking leadership for the Felix G. Woodward Library, ensuring that library services, collections, technologies, staffing, and spaces align with the University’s mission, academic priorities, enrollment goals, student success initiatives, and strategic plan.
Lead and support library faculty and staff through a culture grounded in transparent communication, collaboration, collegiality and mutual respect.
Provide administrative leadership and management for all library service units and related library operations that support innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Develop and implement visionary goals for the library that support teaching, learning, and research goals of the university.
Manage the library’s budget, personnel resources, physical facilities, digital infrastructure, collections, and operational priorities in a strategic, sustainable, and data-informed manner.
Collaborate with academic leadership and divisional campus partners to advance the library’s role in student success and ensure that library resources and services are integrated into the academic life of the University, creating modern, accessible, student-centered physical and virtual library environments.
Lead the continued development of a modern, accessible, student-centered physical and virtual library environments at a public university
Provide leadership in the development, evaluation, preservation, and accessibility of print, digital, archival, and special collections that support APSU’s academic programs, research priorities, and institutional history.
Promote the library as a vibrant intellectual, cultural, and academic commons for students, faculty, staff, alumni, and the broader Clarksville-Montgomery County community.
Lead the library in responding effectively to emerging trends in academic librarianship, including artificial intelligence, digital learning, open science, evolving integrated library systems, metadata and discovery tools, accessibility standards, and new models of information access.
Oversee accreditation and external compliance of the library in consultation with the Associate Director of Library Services.
Advance a culture of inclusion and belonging, maintaining a welcoming library environment for all students, faculty, staff, alumni, and community members.
Recruit, mentor, evaluate, and support the professional growth of library faculty and staff, ensuring that personnel have opportunities to develop expertise in contemporary library practices, technologies, student support, and academic engagement.
Represent the Woodward Library on the Provost’s Leadership Team, University Library Advisory Committee, and the Woodward Library Society Board, as well as in professional organizations, community partnerships, and other internal and external forums, as appropriate, cultivating relationships that support library initiatives.
Cultivate partnerships with alumni, donors, foundations, corporate partners, community organizations, and grant-making entities to support library priorities, special initiatives, collections, facilities, technology, and student-centered programming.
Ensure that library policies and procedures are current, user-centered, equitable, and aligned with professional academic library standards and best practices.
Represent the University and Woodward Library in professional organizations, consortia, community partnerships, state and regional library networks, and other external forums.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

A proven record of success as a collaborative leader and transparent communicator with the ability to develop and convey a compelling vision for the role of the academic library in a changing higher education environment.
Demonstrated knowledge of contemporary issues facing higher education and academic libraries, including intellectual freedom, academic privacy, information /media literacy, scholarly communication, open access, artificial intelligence, digital preservation, and equitable access to library resources and spaces.
A transparent, collaborative, and participatory leadership style that fosters trust, shared purpose, accountability, innovation, and collegiality among library faculty and staff.
Demonstrated ability to manage complex budgets and align financial decisions with institutional priorities, and long-term sustainability.
Demonstrated experience in library assessment, data-informed decision-making, strategic planning, and accreditation support.
A demonstrated commitment to inclusion, belonging, and for all library users of resources, services, and spaces.
Commitment to understanding and addressing the library needs of all undergraduate and graduate students (including traditional, post-traditional, first-generation, and military-affiliated), recognizing a variety of experiences, identities, and perspectives.
The ability to build effective working relationships with faculty, staff, and administrators, alumni, and community partners to advance the mission of the library.
Experience supporting faculty teaching, research, and curriculum development, and the integration of library resources into academic programs.
Ability to foster a positive and productive work environment that supports professional development, faculty and staff engagement, shared governance, and high-quality service.
Demonstrated ability to promote the library’s value and impact through advocacy, communication, outreach, assessment, and relationship-building.
Experience supporting fundraising, grant opportunities, and development efforts that advance library priorities.
Strong communication, interpersonal, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Maintain awareness of national and regional trends in higher education and academic libraries, using that knowledge to guide strategic planning, innovation, resource allocation, and service development.
A deep commitment to academic excellence, student success, faculty support, public service, and the mission of Austin Peay State University.

Minimum Required Qualifications

An ALA-Accredited Master of Library Science or Master's or equivalent degree.
A strong record of achievement in the areas of research, teaching, and service with evidence meriting appointment as the rank of tenured associate or full professor within the Felix G. Woodward Library.
Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible leadership experience in an academic library, preferably within a public university or comprehensive four-year higher education setting.
Demonstrated experience supervising, mentoring, and evaluating library faculty, professional staff and/or support staff.
Demonstrated experience managing library operations, services, budgets, personnel, collections, technologies, and/or facilities.
