new_jobs.title: Managing Director of Donor Operations
new_jobs.description:
Description

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Operational Leadership

Provide senior leadership and overall performance accountability for Donor Services, Donor Recruitment, the Contact Center, and Concierge @Home Donor Services.
Maintain overall accountability for achievement of SunCoast Blood Centers’ blood collection goals and assigned operational objectives.
Lead through departmental directors and managers, ensuring they retain responsibility for their teams, workflows, staffing, scheduling, and routine day-to-day operations.
Establish operational priorities and performance expectations and hold assigned leaders accountable for execution and results.
Ensure assigned departments operate as an integrated collection system, aligning recruitment, appointment generation, staffing, collection capacity, donor engagement, and operational resources with organizational blood needs.
Maintain appropriate visibility into field and center operations to understand performance, identify barriers, and support departmental leaders.
Serve as the senior operational escalation point for issues requiring cross-department coordination, resource decisions, or executive-level intervention.

Collections and Recruitment Strategy

Translate organizational collection goals into clear operational and recruitment priorities across assigned departments.
Provide senior oversight of blood drive recruitment strategy and ensure sufficient collection opportunities are developed to support current and future blood needs.
Ensure successful blood drive accounts are proactively rebooked and developed into recurring partnerships whenever appropriate.
Ensure Recruitment maintains a forward-looking 12-month blood drive calendar designed to support collection goals, strengthen account retention, and identify future collection gaps before they become critical.
Monitor collection performance, recruitment effectiveness, appointment activity, donor trends, and future collection projections and direct corrective strategies when performance is below expectations.
Ensure recruitment strategy is coordinated with staffing capacity, mobile fleet availability, collection locations, and operational resources.
Evaluate mobile and fixed-site collection performance and support changes in deployment, scheduling, locations, or resources when needed to improve collection results.
Support and strengthen relationships with businesses, schools, colleges and universities, healthcare organizations, community groups, and other blood drive partners.

Operational Readiness and Performance

Ensure fixed-site and mobile Donor Services operations have the staffing, equipment, supplies, and resources necessary to safely and effectively achieve collection requirements.
Hold departmental leadership accountable for appropriate inventory management practices, including First-In, First-Out (FIFO) utilization where applicable, to minimize shortages, expired supplies, waste, and avoidable costs.
Ensure Donor Operations equipment is appropriately quality controlled, maintained, and subject to required preventive maintenance in accordance with established procedures and applicable requirements.
Partner with Supply Chain, Quality, Facilities, Information Technology, and other support departments to resolve equipment, supply, technology, fleet, facility, or logistical barriers affecting donor operations.
Provide senior oversight of staffing, labor utilization, overtime, productivity, budgets, and operational expenses and require corrective action when performance is outside expectations.
Provide senior oversight of Concierge @Home performance and ensure the program remains aligned with priority donor and collection needs.
Provide senior oversight of Contact Center performance, including appointment generation, donor engagement, retention, reactivation, and productivity.
Partner with Information Technology and Contact Center leadership to evaluate and implement artificial intelligence, automation, and other technology that improves donor engagement, scheduling, communication, and operational efficiency.

Leadership and Organizational Planning

Develop assigned directors and managers through coaching, performance accountability, professional development, and succession planning.
Build leadership depth by ensuring departmental leaders are appropriately empowered, supported, and accountable within their areas of responsibility.
Participate in annual planning, budgeting, collection forecasting, workforce planning, and organizational goal development.
Maintain operational accountability for compliance with established policies, procedures, safety requirements, and applicable regulatory standards, partnering with Quality and Compliance as appropriate.
Provide the CEO with regular reporting and recommendations regarding collection performance, recruitment pipeline, 12-month blood drive calendar, staffing, productivity, operational readiness, financial performance, risks, and resource needs.
Collaborate with SunCoast Blood Centers leadership to resolve cross-functional barriers and support organizational priorities.

PERFORMANCE EVALUATION METRICS

Performance will be evaluated based on established organizational and departmental goals, including:

Achievement of blood collection goals.
Strength and sustainability of the 12-month blood drive recruitment pipeline, including successful account retention and rebooking.
Staffing, labor productivity, overtime, and operational efficiency.
Mobile and fixed-site collection performance and resource utilization.
Contact Center and Concierge @Home performance in support of collection goals.
Equipment and supply readiness, required QC and preventive maintenance, appropriate inventory practices, and reduction of avoidable waste.
Financial performance within assigned areas.
Development, performance, and accountability of assigned directors and managers.
Ability to anticipate operational needs, resolve barriers, and move donor operations toward proactive and sustainable performance.

Additional Responsibilities

Maintain an active presence at donor centers, mobile blood drives, recruitment activities, schools, colleges and universities, and community locations as operationally appropriate.
Represent SunCoast Blood Centers professionally with donors, blood drive sponsors, community partners, and other external stakeholders.
Participate in meetings, training, professional development, and organizational initiatives as required.
Perform other duties as assigned to support SunCoast Blood Centers’ success.

Physical Requirements

PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL REQUIREMENTS

Prolonged periods of sitting, standing, and computer use.
Ability to occasionally lift up to 30 pounds.
Ability to drive and travel regularly throughout SunCoast Blood Centers’ service area.
Ability to move throughout donor centers, mobile collection environments, and community locations to observe and support operations.

Environmental Requirements

Work is performed in office, donor center, mobile blood drive, school, college/university, and community environments.
May require work at multiple locations within the same day and presence at mobile blood drives with variable weather exposure.
Potential exposure to blood products and biohazardous materials; adherence to applicable safety and infection control standards is required.

Additional Requirements

Must possess and maintain a valid Florida Driver’s License, acceptable driving record, and eligibility to drive on behalf of SunCoast Blood Centers.
When using a personal vehicle for SunCoast Blood Centers business, must maintain automobile insurance as required by Florida law and SunCoast Blood Centers policy.
Must be able to obtain and maintain any background screening, identification, security clearance, or other authorization required for access to schools, colleges, universities, healthcare facilities, or other partner locations.
Regular, reliable, and timely attendance is essential.
Ability to work flexible hours, including occasional early mornings, evenings, weekends, and extended hours based on operational needs.
Ability to respond during emergency operations, disaster events, critical collection needs, or other operational situations as needed.

Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, Management, or a related field preferred. Equivalent relevant leadership experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

Experience

Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive leadership experience in blood banking, blood collection operations, donor services, donor recruitment, or a closely related field.
Minimum of three (3) years of senior-level operational or executive leadership experience with responsibility for directors, managers, or multiple operational functions.
Demonstrated experience leading through other leaders and holding multiple operational functions accountable for measurable results.
Demonstrated experience overseeing blood collection operations, recruitment strategy, staffing, productivity, and operational performance.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong knowledge of blood banking, donor recruitment, donor services, collection operations, and donor experience principles.
Strong understanding of blood drive recruitment, account development and retention, rebooking, and long-term collection planning.
Strong leadership, coaching, decision-making, problem-solving, and team development skills.
Ability to lead effectively through directors and managers while maintaining clear accountability at each leadership level.
Ability to translate organizational goals into actionable operational priorities.
Ability to analyze collection, recruitment, staffing, productivity, labor, logistical, and financial data and take appropriate action based on performance.
Working knowledge of staffing models, budgeting, mobile operations, fleet utilization, inventory practices, technology, and operational resource planning.
Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across departments and with external partners.

CORE COMPETENCIES AND EXPECTATIONS

Maintains accountability for collection performance and assigned operational objectives.
Leads through and develops departmental directors and managers.
Maintains a visible and engaged leadership presence across donor operations.
Anticipates collection needs and promotes proactive planning rather than primarily reactive solutions.
Establishes clear expectations and holds assigned leaders accountable for results.
Uses data, technology, collaboration, and continuous improvement to strengthen performance.
Demonstrates sound judgment, integrity, professionalism, and a mission-focused approach.

Through recent acquisitions, along with strategic partnerships across the life sciences ecosystem, we are accelerating our efforts to advance precision medicine and improve patient outcomes around the world.

At Lantheus we are purpose-driven, and every employee plays a vital role in our success. We’re dedicated to cultivating a high-growth, forward-thinking culture where innovation thrives and diverse perspectives drive meaningful progress.

Join us and be part of a company where your contributions make a real impact, because we know someone’s health is in our hands.

new_jobs.title: Director of External Affairs
new_jobs.description:
About Tennesseans for Student Success

Tennesseans for Student Success (TSS) champions effective education policies that give every Tennessee child access to a quality public education. We combine data, political impact, and the collective power of parents, advocates, and policymakers to make Tennessee the gold standard in public education and to hold leaders accountable for student outcomes.

Building power. Leveraging influence. Changing student lives.

TSS is hiring a Director of External Affairs to own the organization's voice across every channel, earned media, owned media, social, podcast, and our flagship digital outlet. This is not a traditional communications role, and it is not a newsroom role.

We are looking for a strategist and operator who sees communications as an advocacy function that drive public opinion and outcomes: someone who can build narratives that move Tennesseans, legislators, and the policy influencers; produce content that performs across formats; and lead a small team toward measurable advocacy outcomes. The right person thinks like a marketer, writes like a journalist, moves like a campaign comms director, and treats the flagship digital outlet as a powerful platform to advance TSS's policy and political priorities, not as a traditional newsroom operating in a vacuum.

This role reports to executive leadership and manages the communications function, including editorial operations, contractors, and vendors.

What You'll Own

Strategic Direction for a Digital News Outlet
•      Serve as Managing Editor, setting the editorial vision, content calendar, and growth strategy in alignment with TSS's policy and political objectives.
•      Build the outlet into a multi-format platform: articles, podcast, video, social-first content, newsletters, that drives audience growth and shapes the education narrative in Tennessee.
•      Define and track performance metrics: audience growth, engagement, share of voice, narrative penetration, and influence on key audiences (parents, legislators, opinion leaders).
•      Make sharp editorial calls: on story selection, framing, headlines, distribution, and rapid response, that maximize the platform's strategic value.

Integrated Communications & Brand
•      Lead TSS's full communications strategy and daily operations across earned, owned, and paid channels.
•      Develop and enforce organizational messaging, ensuring consistency across TSS, digital news outlet, and affiliated entities.
•      Draft, edit, and approve press releases, op-eds, talking points, newsletters, and public statements.
•      Oversee brand identity, voice, and visual consistency across every public-facing asset.

Digital, Social & Multimedia
•      Direct the social media strategy across all platforms, with a marketer's eye for reach, engagement, and conversion, not just posting.
•      Oversee podcast development, production cadence, guest strategy, and distribution.
•      Manage email marketing and audience-building programs to grow and activate TSS supporter lists.
•      Use analytics to continuously iterate on what's working, and kill what isn't.

Earned Media & Public Relations
•      Serve as the organization's primary media contact and build relationships with reporters, editors, and producers statewide and nationally.
•      Pitch stories, place op-eds, coordinate interviews, and prepare leadership for media engagements.
•      Monitor media coverage and respond quickly and effectively, including in contested or politically charged moments.

Political & Electoral Communications
•      Partner with the political and policy teams to develop sharp, accurate, and well-sourced content during legislative sessions, election cycles, and accountability campaigns.
•      Lead rapid-response messaging when TSS's priorities, allies, or interests are under attack, or when opportunities to advance them emerge.
•      Translate complex policy and political dynamics into clear, persuasive content built for the audience and channel.

Team & Operations
•      Manage communications staff, the editorial team, freelance contributors, and external vendors.
•      Set goals, workflows, and performance expectations; develop talent and elevate the team's work.
•      Manage budgets, vendor relationships, and project timelines.
•      Support crisis communications planning and response.

Who You Are

We are intentionally looking outside the traditional journalism mold. Strong candidates will bring:
•      5+ years in communications, marketing, political/campaign communications, advocacy, or a hybrid of these, with measurable results.
•      A modern, audience-first mindset: you understand how content actually travels in 2026, across social, podcast, video, and email, not just press releases.
•      Marketing instincts. You think in terms of audience, message, channel, and conversion, and you know how to measure what's working.
•      Editorial chops. You can write fast and clean, edit other people's work to a high standard, and make confident calls on framing, headlines, and story selection.
•      Political and advocacy fluency. You're comfortable operating in a mission-driven, electorally active environment and understand how communications drives policy and political outcomes.
•      Multi-format range: comfortable shaping a podcast episode, a Reels script, a long-form op-ed, and a rapid-response thread, or directing others to.
•      Strategic thinking paired with a builder's mentality. You can write a 12-month strategic plan and also ship a campaign by Friday.
•      Leadership experience: you've managed people, contractors, or cross-functional projects and can give clear, direct feedback.
•      Discretion, judgment, and a thick skin. This is a public-facing role in a politically active organization.

Nice to Have

•      Experience with a political campaign, 501(c)(4), PAC, or advocacy organization.
•      Experience launching or scaling a podcast, newsletter, or digital media property.
•      Crisis communications experience.
•      Graphic design, video production, or content creation skills.
•      Familiarity with media monitoring tools, CRM/email platforms, and social analytics.
•      Bachelor's degree in Communications, Marketing, Political Science, Public Relations, Journalism, or a related field. Equivalent professional experience considered.

Logistics

•      Full-time, salaried.
•      Based in Franklin, TN. In-office three days per week.
•      Approximately 25% travel within Tennessee.
•      Some evening and weekend work for events, breaking news, and political moments.
•      Must have a valid driver's license and access to a personal vehicle for work travel.

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive salary commensurate with experience, plus a strong benefits package:
•      Employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance
•      Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Health Savings Account (HSA) options
•      Immediate eligibility for 401(k) with employer match
•      Paid parental leave (maternity, paternity, adoption)
•      Flexible PTO and paid federal and organizational holidays
•      On-site gym

How to Apply

Submit a resume, a brief cover letter, and at least two work samples to TNSShiring@gmail.com. Work samples can be anything that demonstrates your range: a campaign you ran, a podcast you produced, an op-ed you wrote, a social campaign you led, or a piece of accountability content you're proud of. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Develops and implements a comprehensive outreach plan to raise awareness of the Unclaimed Property Program
Works with various divisions across the Treasurer’s Office, including the Legislative Division and Scheduling Division, to partner with and educate members of the General Assembly, elected officials, groups or organizations, and individuals to inform residents of their unclaimed property
Serves as point of contact for unclaimed property outreach initiatives
Interviews and trains employees, plans, assigns, and directs work, appraises performance, and provides positive feedback and constructive criticism to employees

Facilitates a proactive approach to customer satisfaction through the establishment of partnership meetings with key stakeholders.
Demonstrates a hands-on approach for problem solving and solutions and informs management immediately if serious issues arise.
Facilitates the coordination of internal resources to resolve complex problems.
Prepares and/or edits unclaimed property written materials intended for public distribution.
Responds to legislative and constituent inquiries from elected officials and their staff regarding unclaimed property and other Treasurer’s Office programs.

Excellent oral and written communication skills
Ability to interpret data and arrive at appropriate conclusions.
Proficient at prioritizing tasks, working independently, and collaborating across functional areas.
Exhibit good judgment and leverage experience to successfully meet goals.

new_jobs.description:
YOUR POSITION WITH TNC

The Associate Director of Communications, North America Region (NAR) provides strategic, internal and external communications support for a multidisciplinary, regional communications team advancing TNC’s 2030 goals. This role will work closely with NAR leadership teams, Global Communications, Internal Communications, as well as Conservation and Fundraising teams to advise on, design and implement strategic communications initiatives. This work will be aligned to the overarching Marketing and Communications team strategic plan as well as NAR Conservation and Development strategies.

Essential Functions

Reporting to the Director of Marketing, North America Activation and Integration, the Associate Director serves as the strategic communications lead for the region, with a focus on internal communications, executive positioning and organizational alignment. This role partners closely with NAR leadership including the Regional Executive Director, the Managing Director of Operational Excellence, other senior leaders and their teams, as well as the Global Director of Internal Communications to shape and deliver integrated communications that advance regional priorities and TNC’s 2030 goals.

The Associate Director leads strategic communications planning and execution, prioritizing clear and consistent engagement with internal audiences while supporting external positioning as needed. They align messaging across the region and with global teams, strengthen leadership communications and ensure employees, partners and key stakeholders are informed and engaged. The role serves as a trusted advisor to the Regional Executive Director and senior leadership, providing counsel on approach, tone and timing for high-impact communications. They provide strategic counsel and media preparation for senior leaders, including message development, interview preparation and spokesperson support for media engagements.

This position manages complex, cross-functional initiatives, builds strong relationships with marketing and communications leaders and key stakeholders and establishes processes that drive coordination and clarity. They also guide regional response planning for sensitive issues to help protect organizational reputation. External and media engagement is aligned to broader strategy and supports regional priorities.

Responsibilities & Scope

Develop and execute strategic communications plan for NAR office.
Create talking points, FAQs, backgrounders and other critical communications collateral impacting the NAR.
Cultivate deep understanding of NAR conservation priorities and programs.
Advise on and execute NAR communications rollouts related to finance, operations, policy communications, change management, and other internal/external moments impacting staff.
Provides leadership and connectivity between TNC teams for internal, executive, policy and crisis communications for the NAR.
Supports rapid response communications involving both internal and external audiences.
Aligns NAR communications with global Marketing and Communications team strategies and initiatives with regards to messaging, sequencing and strategic direction.
Along with other key communications stakeholders, provides input for NAR responses using TNC’s rapid response framework and internal decision-making tools.
Works closely with TNC’s Global Director of Internal Communications to align NAR internal communications strategy with the global approach.
Supports executive communications for key NAR leadership.
Provides communications, technical, and 'on-air' support for NAR management team for townhalls, all staff conversations, conservation learning sessions and division-wide calls when needed.
Regularly updates NAR internal/external collateral including SharePoint pages, backgrounders and impact reports.
Provides support for senior NAR leaders' internal and external presentations.
Social media strategy/support for NAR Regional Executive Director.
Develops NAR communications materials for leadership team that aligns with TNC’s One Future campaign.
Responsibility and accountability for meeting strategic goals and objectives.
Demonstrates flexibility and responsiveness in support of executive communications, leadership priorities, and time-sensitive organizational initiatives, including work outside of standard business hours when needed.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in related field and a minimum of 8 years related experience or equivalent combination.
Experience developing complex integrated strategic communications plans.
Experience measuring results of strategic plans and programs.
Experience cultivating and managing relationships with senior level executives, board members and members of the media.
Experience supporting earned media efforts, including preparing executives for media interviews and appearances.

Desired Qualifications

Senior level experience in communications field.
Excellent writing, presentation, communication, mediation and negotiation skills.
Experience managing organizational change management and advising senior leaders.
Experience coordinating with stakeholders across a global organization and with cross-functional global teams.
Experience developing, implementing, measuring and evaluating multifaceted strategic communications initiatives, plans and programs.
Proven success in building and maintaining long-term relationships with partners, board members, senior leaders and members of the media.
Proven ability in managing the fiduciary aspects of planning and delivery of annual budgets.

This description is not designed to be a complete list of all duties and responsibilities required for this job.

Salary Information

The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $82,790 - $124,270
. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

NOTICE OF JOB POSTING

POSITION TITLE: COMMUNITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR

COMMUNITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT

NON-UNION – GRADE 15

FULL-TIME

PAY RANGE: $113,713.72 TO $152,849.32 PER YEAR

Position Overview

Under general administrative direction from the Town Manager, plans, directs, manages, and oversees the functions, programs, and operations of the Community and Economic Development/Planning Department including community and economic development, planning, zoning, and state and federal grants assistance.

The Community and Economic Development Director is responsible for the development, recommendation, and implementation of policies, programs, and procedures that accomplish the goals and objectives established by the Town Manager and Town Council to ensure the continued growth and economic health and vitality of the Town. Ensuring direct collaboration with residents and businesses in Town along with other Town departments.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Assumes full management responsibility for all department functions, programs and operations, including economic development, community relations and special events.
Manages the day-to-day operations of the department; initiates studies regarding zoning issues, development of ordinances, business regulations, review of permits, architectural designs, etc.
Plans, coordinates and directs the implementation of the Town Master Plan with elected and appointed officials.
Oversees land use planning policies and procedures, including the review of development projects.
Responsible for the oversight of various functions within the CED Department, which includes the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, Conservation Commission, and open space programs and policies.
Participates on a variety of boards, commissions, committees, and teams; reviews and prepares public presentations at Town Council and other public meetings; participates in Town Council directed projects/teams including Council Subcommittees, Economic Development, and projects of major importance to the Town.
Assists with applying for, obtaining and administering federal and state grants.
Performs related duties as assigned by the Town Manager.

Qualificiations

Necessary Knowledge and Skills:

Thorough knowledge of the principles and practices of local planning and development; planning, zoning, wetlands regulations, design and subdivision law, theory and applications; local government structure and operation, including budgetary procedures.
Considerable knowledge of modern principles and practices of municipal government.
Demonstrated skill in procuring and managing grants.
Skill in public relations; making presentations, writing reports and other communication practices.
Skill in general office management and practices, interpersonal communication, employee supervision, motivation, and the ability to direct the work of others.
Demonstrated proficiency in the use of computers and office software applications including spreadsheet applications.

Ability To

Ability to oversee and manage the financial operations of the Community and Economic Development Department, including budgeting, accounting and financial reporting.
Ability to coordinate ongoing projects.
Ability to effectively manage the full life cycle of grants, from identification and application to administration, compliance and reporting.
Effective communication skills. Must be able to present financial information clearly to stakeholders, collaborate with team members, and provide financial guidance and recommendations.

Education And Experience

Graduation from college with a Bachelor’s Degree in urban planning, public administration, economic development, public policy or closely related field and eight (8) years of experience performing above or related duties, to include three (3) years in progressively responsible experience planning, implementing and overseeing the economic development activities, or an equivalent combination of education and/or experience.
Master’s degree is preferred. Knowledge of municipal development processes and experience interacting with local government entities and officials strongly preferred.
American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP) certification or Certified Economic Developer (CEcD) is preferred.
Working knowledge of Geographic Information Systems (ARC/Info) is highly desirable.

What We Can Achieve Together

The Managing Director, Data, AI & Applied Technology advances The Nature Conservancy (TNC)'s conservation mission by defining how data, applied technology, and artificial intelligence create measurable mission and business value. This is a newly created role and a first-of-its-kind function at TNC: it owns the “what, who, and why” of data, applied technology, and AI, including what decisions must improve, what outcomes matter most, where data can create mission advantage, and how emerging technologies should be responsibly explored and applied. The role then translates these insights into coordinated, collaborative execution to deliver measurable outcomes.

This role leads enterprise business data strategy, domain data ownership, data governance accountability, responsible AI governance, use-case prioritization, value realization, and adoption, and partners closely with the CIO organization, which owns technical data platforms, architecture, engineering, controls, and scalable delivery.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer with a dotted line to the Chief Executive Officer, and a dotted-line partnership with the Chief Information Officer, the Managing Director serves as TNC's senior authority on business data and AI strategy and governance, applied and emerging conservation technology, the NatureChat and conservation intelligence workstreams, technology partnerships, and external thought leadership and cross-NGO positioning.

In This Role, You Will

Develop and maintain TNC's enterprise business data, applied technology, and AI strategies, aligned to conservation priorities and organizational goals.
Establish and mature a federated domain data ownership model across Conservation, Science, Development/Membership, Marketing, HR, Finance, Legal, Operations, and other enterprise domains.
Lead enterprise data governance from a business accountability perspective, and establish responsible AI governance guidance, acceptable-use expectations, and risk-review processes.
Build executive and domain-leader commitment to data stewardship, data quality, responsible AI, and adoption, and develop data and AI literacy programs in partnership with People, Learning, IT, and business domains.
Build and manage a high-performing, globally aware team spanning business data strategy and governance, responsible AI, portfolio management, adoption, and data culture.
Operate as an enterprise partner and trusted advisor to the Executive Leadership Team, and represent TNC in external forums on responsible AI, conservation data, and mission-driven data strategy.
Manage an annual operating budget covering team, tools, and external services, and negotiate and manage contracts with vendors and service partners.

You will navigate the unique dynamics of a globally federated organization, building consensus across regions and business units while maintaining enterprise standards, and champion a culture where people at every level can confidently use data to make decisions.

This position is hybrid, with a preference for candidates based in the Washington, DC metro area near TNC's Arlington, VA office, though flexibility exists for candidates located elsewhere.

Bachelor's degree in business, law, data science, data governance, natural resource management, or other relevant field and 10 or more years of experience, including 5 years of experience at a senior level in a global and/or multi-product line organization, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Experience translating organizational strategy into data, analytics, applied technology, or AI-enabled business outcomes.
Experience with executive-level communication and influence, including building credibility with non-technical senior audiences and technical partners.
Experience leading governance, decision rights, adoption strategies, change management, and benefits realization across a matrixed organization.
Experience with data privacy, security, ethical data use, responsible AI, and inclusive change leadership.

Experience in global, federated, or mission-driven organizations.
Experience establishing federated data governance, responsible AI governance, domain data ownership, or data product operating models.
Familiarity with conservation science data, geospatial data, fundraising or donor data, marketing data, HR or people data, finance data, or comparable complex data domains.
Track record building organizational data literacy and adoption, encompassing culture and behavior change, not just tools.

Full-time Description

Chief Executive Officer (CEO)

Lead an Organization Devoted to the Strength of Family

The Family Initiative, Inc. (TFI) is seeking an accomplished and visionary leader to serve as its next Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
. This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a mission-driven organization dedicated to strengthening children, families, and communities through innovative services, advocacy, and operational excellence.

The CEO serves as the chief executive and strategic leader of The Family Initiative, Inc. and its affiliated organizations, guiding a multi-state enterprise that delivers child welfare, behavioral health, family support, technology, and nonprofit support services. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CEO is responsible for advancing the organization's mission, ensuring financial sustainability, fostering organizational excellence, and positioning TFI for continued growth and impact.

About The Family Initiative, Inc.

The Family Initiative, Inc. is the parent organization providing services to children and families across the United States through its affiliates:

TFI Family Services (Kansas, Nebraska, and Missouri)
TFI Family Connections (Oklahoma)
Texas Family Initiative (Texas)
Pathway Family Services (Kansas and Texas)
Mainstream Nonprofit Solutions, providing shared services and nonprofit support
Foster Care Technologies, delivering technology solutions for child welfare organizations

TFI is a private, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization governed by a voluntary Board of Directors committed to strengthening families and improving outcomes for children and communities.

Position Summary

The Chief Executive Officer provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for the TFI Family of Companies. The CEO partners closely with the Board of Directors to establish organizational priorities, guide long-term planning, ensure financial stewardship, and advance the mission and vision of the organization.

This leader will oversee a complex and growing enterprise, ensuring high-quality service delivery, regulatory compliance, organizational stability, and strong relationships with community partners, funders, government agencies, and other key stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Develop and execute long-term strategic plans in partnership with the Board of Directors.
Establish organizational goals, priorities, and policies that support mission achievement and sustainable growth.
Lead organizational innovation and identify opportunities for expansion and service enhancement.
Guide strategic initiatives, partnerships, mergers, acquisitions, or other growth opportunities.

Board Partnership and Governance

Serve as Chair of the Executive Team and an ex-officio member of all Board committees.
Support the Board's governance responsibilities through timely communication, planning, and policy recommendations.
Advise the Board on strategic, operational, financial, and regulatory matters.

Operational Excellence

Ensure effective administration of programs, services, and organizational operations.
Monitor organizational performance and implement corrective actions when necessary.
Promote efficiency, accountability, continuous improvement, and organizational effectiveness.

Financial Stewardship

Provide oversight of budgeting, financial planning, and fiscal management.
Ensure the long-term financial health and sustainability of the organization.
Monitor financial performance and maintain strong internal controls and risk management practices.

External Relations and Advocacy

Serve as the primary spokesperson and ambassador for the organization.
Build and maintain strong relationships with government agencies, community partners, legislators, funders, and stakeholders.
Represent the organization in public forums, legislative matters, community events, and media engagements.

Organizational Culture and Talent Leadership

Foster a culture grounded in TFI's mission, vision, and values.
Recruit, develop, and retain high-performing leaders and teams.
Champion diversity, inclusion, collaboration, and professional development throughout the organization.

Compliance and Risk Management

Ensure compliance with applicable local, state, and federal laws and regulations.
Maintain effective policies, procedures, and systems of organizational accountability.
Oversee organizational risk management efforts and ensure operational integrity.

Qualifications/Required Qualifications

Master's degree in social work, business administration, public administration, or a related field is required
Minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience within child welfare, behavioral health, human services, or related fields.
Senior executive leadership experience with responsibility for organizational strategy, operations, and financial oversight.
Demonstrated success in financial management, including budgeting, fiscal planning, and stewardship of organizational resources.
Experience working effectively with Boards of Directors, government agencies, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Experience managing government-funded programs.

Preferred Qualifications

Multi-state organizational leadership experience.
Experience leading multi-entity or complex organizational structures.
Experience operating in one or more TFI service states.
Experience within a Community-Based Care (CBC), Single Source Continuum Contractor (SSCC), or similar service delivery model.
Demonstrated success leading organizational growth, transformation, or expansion initiatives.

The Ideal Candidate

The Successful Candidate Will Demonstrate

Strategic Thinking

The ability to navigate complexity, evaluate data and financial information, anticipate challenges, and establish a clear direction for the future.

Operational Agility

A disciplined and adaptable leader who can execute strategy, ensure compliance, and respond effectively to changing environments.

Interpersonal Savvy

A relationship-focused executive who builds trust, communicates effectively, negotiates skillfully, and inspires confidence.

People Leadership

A leader who develops others, cultivates talent, and fosters alignment around a shared mission and vision.

Travel Requirements

This position requires significant travel, including regional and overnight travel, to organizational locations, Board meetings, community events, legislative functions, and stakeholder engagements.

Compensation And Benefits

Compensation is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience.

TFI Offers a Comprehensive Benefits Package, Including

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Retirement benefits
Paid time off
Employee assistance programs
Professional development opportunities
Additional employee benefits and wellness resources

Qualified candidates are encouraged to submit a resume and cover letter through TFI's online employment application system. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

If you are a mission-driven executive leader with a passion for improving the lives of children and families, we invite you to explore this opportunity to lead one of the nation's premier family service organizations.
